title: Family, early music and Carrollton
summary: No musicians in his family, though they were singers; he followed parades and second lines as a boy and lived around Carrollton.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, was that almost a separate town in those days, I guess? Oh, yeah. Can you tell us about your family a little, if they played music, your father and mother?

Well, I had an uncle that told me, used to try to play trumpet. But I mean, he didn't care too much, you know what I mean, about it. In other words, he wasn't a professional musician. Yeah. And so I don't know of anybody else in my family that played music.
You didn't play in any of the bands then, that anybody around remembers him much in any band?
And your father didn't play anything then?
No, he didn't play any instruments at all.
Your mother sang or anything? I guess they all sang a little bit.
Oh, yeah. They were great singers. They used to have quartets and different things like that, you know.
They were great singers, I mean. But so far as playing music, well, I don't remember any one of them playing music.
Can you remember the first music you ever heard where it was or what kind of, was it bands or parades or music in churches or home or place?
Well, I used to hear a lot of bands. I mean, these parades, you know what I mean, and different things like that, and the second lines. I used to follow the parade when I was a little kid.
How long did you live in Carlton?

Did you live there for years? Well, yeah, for years. I lived in Carlton until I was old enough to, you know, go out on my own, most likely. Of course, we lived around, you know, different sections of the city, too, you know.
We moved in different places, you know. And then we ended up right back up in Carlton again.
